skill.name: daily-meeting-update
skill.description: Generate daily standup updates through a guided interview, with optional context from approved GitHub, Git, Jira, and Claude Code activity.
skill.summary: Create concise Markdown standup updates from interview answers and approved developer activity.
skill.author: softaworks

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, sample GitHub links, and ordinary standup wording. Confirmed risk is limited to privacy-sensitive local access to Claude Code history under ~/.claude/projects; no prompt injection or network exfiltration was found.

remediation.issue: Claude Code history detection touches a hidden home directory.
remediation.suggestion: Ask for explicit permission before probing ~/.claude/projects, not only before reading session details.

remediation.issue: Digest output can expose private local development metadata.
remediation.suggestion: Redact project paths, file names, and first-message text by default unless the user selects them.

remediation.issue: External tool checks may inspect user-specific GitHub or Jira state.
remediation.suggestion: Keep CLI commands read-only, scope them to approved repositories, and explain each command before running it.

content.value_statement: Daily updates take time and often miss context from developer tools. This skill interviews you and turns approved GitHub, Jira, and Claude Code activity into Markdown.
actual_capabilities: Conducts a four-question interview covering yesterday, today, blockers, and discussion topics.
Detects optional GitHub, Git, Jira, and Claude Code integrations before offering them.
Asks for user approval before pulling GitHub, Jira, or Claude Code activity data.
Summarizes Claude Code sessions with titles, projects, branches, touched files, and command counts.
Lets users select relevant Claude Code sessions before including them in the update.
Produces a concise Markdown daily update with sections for work, blockers, reviews, and links.
limitations: GitHub and Jira context requires configured local tools or MCP access.
Claude Code history requires local JSONL session files and user approval.
The generated update depends on accurate user answers during the interview.
It does not send the update to chat, email, or calendar tools automatically.

use_cases.title: Prepare a developer standup
use_cases.description: Turn recent work, planned tasks, blockers, and discussion topics into a short daily update.

use_cases.title: Collect context across repositories
use_cases.description: Combine approved GitHub, Git, Jira, and Claude Code activity from multiple projects.

use_cases.title: Recall work outside ticket systems
use_cases.description: Use selected Claude Code session summaries to remember research, debugging, and planning work.

prompt_templates.title: Basic daily update
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me prepare my daily standup update. Ask me the standard questions and format the final answer in Markdown.

prompt_templates.title: Daily with GitHub context
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare my standup update and ask whether to include recent GitHub or Git activity from my current project.

prompt_templates.title: Daily with Jira planning
prompt_templates.prompt: Create my daily update. If Jira is available, ask before checking assigned tickets and use them as context.

prompt_templates.title: Multi-source team update
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a concise standup update using approved GitHub, Jira, and Claude Code history. Let me choose what to include.

output_examples.input: I fixed the login timeout, reviewed two pull requests, and will continue OAuth work today.
output_examples.output: Daily Update: Yesterday, fixed the login timeout and reviewed two pull requests. Today, continue OAuth work. Blockers: none.

output_examples.input: Use my approved GitHub activity and ask me for blockers and discussion topics.
output_examples.output: Daily Update: Yesterday, merged the login fix and opened the OAuth pull request. Today, deploy to staging. Discussion: payment architecture.

output_examples.input: Include selected Claude Code sessions for yesterday and keep the update short.
output_examples.output: Daily Update: Yesterday, debugged authentication, researched payment providers, and prepared OAuth changes. Today, finish integration testing. Blockers: credentials pending.

best_practices: Approve only the repositories, tickets, and Claude Code sessions that belong in the meeting update.
Answer the interview questions with outcomes, not only task names or ticket numbers.
Review the final Markdown before sharing it with a team or manager.
anti_patterns: Do not include personal projects or private experiments in the selected activity list.
Do not skip the blockers and discussion questions when preparing for a real meeting.
Do not paste raw commit messages when a short human summary is clearer.

faq.question: Does this skill work without integrations?
faq.answer: Yes. It can run as a manual interview and produce a Markdown update from your answers.

faq.question: What integrations can it use?
faq.answer: It can use GitHub CLI, local Git, Jira CLI, Atlassian MCP, and Claude Code session history when available.

faq.question: Will it read my Claude Code history automatically?
faq.answer: The workflow asks for approval before running the digest script or including session history in the update.

faq.question: Can I choose which sessions appear in the update?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow presents Claude Code sessions for selection before adding them to the standup summary.

faq.question: What format does it produce?
faq.answer: It produces Markdown with sections for yesterday, today, blockers, reviews, tickets, topics, and links.

faq.question: Is the final update shared automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill generates text for you to review and share manually.
